findings.details: [P2] Preserve the active polling-check actor when adding a pause. inFlight recognizes claimed Agent work and running Script/Fetch nodes, but a polling Wait deliberately stays waiting while its Script/Fetch check executes in localJobs. Adding a library/workflow hold during that check therefore emits waiting.kind pause, actor person and a pause blocker even though the engine process is still progressing and can finish without intervention. The inspector also labels it Paused. This violates AC7 and the documented person-only-when-all-progress-needs-intervention rule. /tmp/interlock-230-review-boundary.mts launches a real check, observes its ready file, adds a hold, captures the incorrect briefing, then verifies completion exactly once and downstream gating; its explicit actor assertion fails in /tmp/interlock-230-review-boundary.log. Track/project in-flight checks consistently, preserve engine actor until they settle, and cover this transition including waited-parent rollup.

[P2] Separate acknowledged pause creation from follow-up refresh failure. perform awaits action and load in the same try, so when pauses.pause succeeds and pauses.list fails, catch reports a generic failure while the original actor/reason and add form remain. Retry refresh reveals the committed hold but leaves Pause workflow enabled with those same values; clicking it retries the apparently failed action and creates a second independent hold UUID. The fresh UI review demonstrated duplicateHoldCount 2 with actual controls, and I independently inspected journey-interruption.js, journey-interruption-continuation.log and add-recovered-duplicate-action-1440.png under .tasks/issue-230/ui-review-e8f29994. Acknowledged writes need a completed add state and a read-only refresh retry; preserve inputs for actual write failures without turning refresh recovery into another create. Keep independent explicit Add another pause behavior.
